title: Saudi Arabia Electric Vehicle Market Size, Share, Growth, and Forecast 2026-2035 | Vision 2030 and Fleet Electrification Propel 25.10% CAGR Toward USD 5.53 Billion
author: Researchandmarkets.Com
description: Saudi Arabia's EV market is projected to grow at a 25.10% CAGR from 2026-2035, reaching USD 5.53 billion by 2035, driven by Vision 2030 initiatives, fleet electrification, domestic manufacturing, and charging infrastructure development. Battery electric vehicles and passenger cars are expected to lead growth, with major automakers competing through localized production, climate-adapted engineering, and fleet-focused strategies.

title: Ford Motor Company (F) Stock Falls Amid Market Uptick: What Investors Need to Know
author: Zacks.Com
description: Ford Motor Company's stock fell 1.97% to $12.19 on October 19, 2026, underperforming the broader market's 0.41% gain. The company faces headwinds with a 5.9% monthly decline and expected EPS down 13.33% for the upcoming quarter, though full-year earnings are projected to rise 70.64%. Ford holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with a Forward P/E of 6.69, trading at a significant discount to its industry average.

title: General Motors Pre-Q3 Analysis: Is the Stock a Buy Now?
author: Na
description: General Motors is expected to report Q3 2026 EPS of $3.55, up 26.7% year-over-year, extending its 16-quarter earnings beat streak. Despite a 5.5% decline in U.S. vehicle sales, disciplined pricing and growing software revenues support profitability. However, commodity inflation, logistics costs, and onshoring expenses pose near-term headwinds. GM maintains a Hold rating due to strong fundamentals offset by cost pressures.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: GM shows strong earnings growth potential with 26.7% EPS increase and consistent beat streak, supported by disciplined pricing and software expansion. However, near-term cost pressures from inflation, logistics, and onshoring, combined with declining U.S. vehicle sales, create offsetting headwinds. The Hold rating reflects balanced strengths and risks.

title: Rivian's Key to Success May Not Be Its Vehicles
author: Catie Hogan
description: Rivian's most valuable opportunity may lie in its robotics venture rather than vehicle sales. The company owns approximately one-third of Mind Robotics, an AI-enabled manufacturing technology company founded by Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe. Mind recently hired Doug Field, a veteran executive from Tesla and Ford, as president. With a stake valued at over $1 billion and $1 billion in recent funding, Mind Robotics could provide significant returns for Rivian investors if successful, though Rivian's EV business still needs to achieve profitability.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The article highlights a significant growth opportunity through Mind Robotics ownership, which could be highly lucrative. Additionally, Rivian achieved record Q3 deliveries of 19,248 vehicles and launched its more affordable R2 fleet, demonstrating operational progress despite stock underperformance.
